MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS
  MONDAY, JUNE 2, 2025

1.  CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Nicklas

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

  Also present:  Stephen A. McEwen, Assistant City Attorney

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MAY 5, 2025

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSIONER MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 5, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL SUCH
  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250146; ADDRESS: 2215 Potrillo Road, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Nareg Ghazarian, Red Arch LA; DESCRIPTION: A request
  for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250147) for a single-story addition to a
  single-story residence, and a Variance (V-250148) for an addition that will be built within a
  required front yard and projects beyond the existing forwardmost building line.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-250146 summarizing
the staff report. She provided an overview of the existing property and added that there have been
recent improvements to the home that were approved ministerially, which includes revising the pool,

  1

June 2, 2025
 a small addition to the rear, and a covered patio at the back of the property. The proposed project is
a 172 sq. ft. single story addition, which expands into the front yard. She further explained the
configuration of the property, which per code classifies the side yard as the front yard. Staff has
determined that the project meets the criteria for Neighborhood Compatibility and the findings to
support the Variance can be met based on the configuration of the lot and the development patterns
of the neighborhood.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution
No. PA-250146, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Michael Bailey, Property Owner, stated that as mentioned in the presentation, the front of the house
is actually the side yard, and stated that the proposed addition would be helpful.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250146 AS PRESENTED

AYES: Olson, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT: Nicklas
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No. PA-
250146, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250147) for a single-story addition to a single-story
residence, and a Variance (V-250148) for an addition that will be built within a required front yard and
projects beyond the existing forwardmost building line at 2215 Portrillo Road. There is a 20-day
appeal period where the City Council by its own motion or any member of the public may appeal this
project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250040; ADDRESS: 11 Peacock Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Nareg Ghazarian, Red Arch LA; DESCRIPTION: A request
  for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250041) for first- and second-story
  additions to a two-story residence, a Grading Application (G-250042) for cut of more than 3
  feet in depth and the export of more than 20 cubic yards of earth material, and a Variance (V-
  250043) for an addition that will be built within a required front yard and projects beyond the
  existing forwardmost building line.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-250040 summarizing
the staff report. She stated that there are permits for work currently under construction at the site,
including an interior remodel with window replacements and a 412 SQ. FT. addition towards the west
side and rear yard. The proposed project is a 100 SQ. FT. single story addition at the front of the
house and a 140 SQ. FT. second story addition on the west side of the house. The project also
includes grading at the rear to create new retaining walls to accommodate a new patio and BBQ
area. She stated that the project conforms with the criteria for Neighborhood Compatibility; staff
believe that the findings to support the Variance can be met due to the flat configuration and deep
setback of the lot; and staff found that the project meets the criteria to approve a Grading application.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution
No. PA-250040, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if the front setback is the front 25 ft. of the driveway.
Senior Planner Berry stated that the code addresses front setbacks in different ways, but there is a
  2
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 2, 2025
 minimum set back of 25 ft. However, the code also defines the front yard of all residential lots as the
area between the front property line and the front building façade; which in this case, the entire 160
ft. length of the property is considered the front yard.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that this seems punitive for property owners who have
oversized properties and have opted to push their properties far enough back to create an “artificial
front yard”. She asked if staff have considered an ordinance amendment that would allow for some
flexibility in this requirement. Director Naughton stated that this is one of the items that will be coming
before the Commission in terms of revisions to our residential district standards.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Daniel Swisher, Property Owner, explained the need for the proposed improvements to his property
including providing for a new entry way, additional bathrooms for his family, and in the rear a BBQ
area without losing the grass area where his kids play.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about access during construction. Mr. Swisher stated that this
will happen from his street, and not from the Dapplegray neighborhood since this would be more
difficult.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about staging for construction since the property is within a cul-
de-sac. Mr. Swisher stated that the construction will be maintained within his property and stated
that the property has a large driveway to accommodate staging for construction.

Mark Azarian, Designer, welcomed any further questions about the project.

There were no further questions.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. PA-250040 IN ACCORDANCE WITH CEQA REQUIREMENTS.

AYES: Olson, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT: Nicklas
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No. PA-
20040, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for first- and second-story additions to a two-story
residence, a Grading Application for cut of more than 3 feet in depth and the export of more than 20
cubic yards of earth material, and a Variance for an addition that will be built within a required front
yard and projects beyond the existing forwardmost building line at 11 Peacock Lane. There is a 20-
day appeal period where the City Council by its own motion or any member of the public may appeal
this project.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250082; ADDRESS:4651 Marloma Drive, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: John Juge, Arch-Scape LLC; DESCRIPTION: A request for
  a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (ND-250083) for a 1,419 square foot single-story
  residential addition, a Variance (V-250084) for a single-story addition built along
  nonconforming side yard setbacks that were approved through Variance 104-63, and two
  Minor Deviations for a covered front porch that encroaches into the front yard not further than
  the forwardmost building line (MD-250087) and will decrease the required front yard area by
  less than 10% (MD-250088).

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-250082 summarizing
the staff report. She explained improvements that have been made to the home and stated that the
  3
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 2, 2025
 proposed project includes a 1,419 sq. ft. single story addition and a new 434 sq. ft. covered patio at
the rear of the residence; the existing septic tank system will be relocated further back on the
property; and a new covered porch in the front is proposed to be centrally located to create a
welcoming entry for the residents.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff is of the opinion that this proposal conforms to the
Neighborhood Compatibility ordinance and the findings to support the Variance based on the
substandard width of the lot, and staff can support the Minor Deviation because the proposal is
consistent with the city's general plan and does not conflict with any other provisions of the zoning
ordinance and does not adversely affect surrounding properties.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution
No. PA-250082, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON disclosed that the applicant, John Juge is a longtime friend of his, and
stated that he has not discussed this project with him, and believes he does not have any conflict of
interest; however, if there is any objection he would recuse himself from the discussion and the
vote.

There were no objections.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if in the past have additions continue to be allowed in non-
conforming setbacks and if there is a precedent on how these are treated.

Director Naughton stated that typically these would be processed as a Minor Deviation at the
administrative level. The property was developed under LA County development standards prior to
the City’s incorporation. There is a Minor Deviation provision in the code that allows the continuation
along that same non-conforming building line; however, in this case, there was a Variance granted a
few short years after the City incorporated and the procedural pathway of amending the Variance
had to be followed.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Sherri Nixon, Property Owner explained the need for improvements to her home including more room
for her growing family, creating a welcoming front yard entry way, a great room for their family to
gather, and additional bathrooms.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the relocation of the septic system. Director Naughton
stated that this will be addressed during the building permit process and the applicant will also need
to work with Los Angeles County Environmental Health for abandonment and relocation of the septic
tank.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250082 AS PRESENTED.

AYES: Olson, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

 area by less than 10% at 4651 Marloma Drive. There is a 20-day appeal period where the City Council

D.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250001; ADDRESS:82 Dapplegray Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Kelsey Fair, Fair Studios/HRS; DESCRIPTION: A request
  for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250002) for rear yard improvements, a
  Grading Permit (G-250003) for the import of more than 20 cubic yards of earth materials for
  fill greater than three feet in vertical height at its deepest point, a Variance to exceed lot
  coverage by more than 10% (V-250004) and a Variance to waive the requirement to designate
  a future horse keeping area on the site plan (V-250081).

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-250169 summarizing
the staff report. She stated that at the previous meeting the Planning Commission expressed their
concerns with the fact that the property is undesirable for horse keeping given its substandard size
and acknowledged that the property owner and applicant has no intention of keeping horses at the
site. The applicant has worked with staff to evaluate all potential locations of a minimum 800 sq. ft.
foot horse keeping area that would be a minimum of 12 feet in width or length and 35 feet from any
dwelling and meet all the other development standards for horse keeping. It was determined that the
only possible location on the site that could accommodate such an area is the northeast corner of
the property extending along the rear property line and the plan has been revised to show the
proposed project.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take public testimony,
discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution No. PA-250169 approving the
project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that in his opinion approving this Variance would essentially
eliminate the horse keeping area due to the construction of the pool and an ADU; someone could
conceivably buy the property and remove the pool and the ADU for a horse keeping area.

Senior Planner Berry stated that because the property is in the horse overlay zone, it allows that
property to enjoy the right to keep horses there. This approval would allow the applicant to waive the
code requirement to show an 800 square foot area on their on their site plan where they could
conceivably keep horses. This approval does not change the fact that there is a right that the property
keep horses and addresses the concerns that were raised at the last Planning Commission about
the location of the horse keeping area.

COMMISSIONER OLSON quoted the horse lot preservation provisions of the zoning code where a
property owner can request a Variance from the horse lot preservation requirements if they would
suffer unique hardship due to the implementation of the requirements of this section because of
size, location, topography, shape or special circumstances. He asked how unique hardships are
defined.

ASSISTANT CITY ATTORNEY MCEWEN stated that it is on a case-by-case determination based
on the particular circumstances of the property. He stated that in this case, staff have found that it is
supportable due to the unique circumstance of the size of the lot. It is up to the Planning
Commission to determine whether the circumstances rise to this level.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Brian Little, property owner, stated that he had no new comments except to say thank you for the
Planning Commission’s consideration and thanked staff for all their work.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI commended Mr. Little on acting on the suggestion of the Planning
Commission to send a letter to their neighbor addressing their concerns.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

 A brief discussion ensued.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about the average size of homes in the horse overlay
zone. Senior Planner Whitney stated that she will need to come back with this information and
explained that a project that had a similar issue was approved recently.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN questioned the need for the Variance due to the construction
of the ADU. Director Naughton explained that the required horse keeping area is being reduced in
size from what the code requires, and a Variance is needed.

Further discussion ensued.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  ADOPT PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250001 BASED ON STAFF’S FINDING.

AYES: Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES: Olson
ABSENT: Nicklas
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No. PA-
20001, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for rear yard improvements, a Grading Permit for the
import of more than 20 cubic yards of earth materials for fill greater than three feet in vertical height
at its deepest point, a Variance to exceed lot coverage by more than 10% and a Variance to waive
the requirement to designate a future horse keeping area on the site plan at 82 Dapplegray Lane.
There is a 20-day appeal period where the City Council by its own motion or any member of the
public may appeal this project.

E.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250169; ADDRESS: Citywide; APPLICANT: City of
  Rolling Hills Estates; DESCRIPTION: An Ordinance of the City of Rolling Hills Estates,
  California, amending and restating Chapters 17.56, 17.80, and 16.06, of the City of Rolling
  Hills Estates Municipal Code pertaining to the regulation of Accessory Dwelling Units, Urban
  Dwelling Units, and Urban Lot Splits.

Director Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-250169 summarizing the staff report. She
provided background on significant changes during the 2023/2024 legislative session. Director
Naughton stated that all single-family residences in the horse overlay zone are now exempt from the
provisions of SB9. This applies to horse keeping zones designated in a master plan adopted prior to
January 1, 1994.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues related to Zoning Text Amendment ZTA 250205;
close the public hearing; and adopt Resolution No. PA-250169, recommending to the City Council
the adoption of amendments to Chapters 16.06, 17.56, and 17.80 of the Rolling Hills Estates
Municipal Code pertaining to Urban Lot Splits and the regulation of Accessory Dwelling Units and
Urban Dwelling Units, and determining the code amendments are exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked for clarification on section 17.56.050 in regard to multifamily
units not to exceed eight units. Director Naughton stated that State law previously read that a
multifamily property could have 25% of the number of existing multifamily units ADU’s; this bill has
clarified that it is up to eight as long as eight is not more than the existing number of multifamily units
on the property and up to two for a proposed multifamily dwelling. Currently, only CGMU and our
CLMU districts allow for multifamily residential or an RPD; however, RPD needs to go through a
separate discretionary process in order for that kind of master-planned type development to occur on
a site.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if an existing multifamily property proposes up to the
eight units, would they typically be removing parking in order to get those additional units or taking
over like the common area space. Director Naughton stated that this could be the case and if there
is an HOA, they would still need to deal with the CC&R’s on a civil level.

A brief discussion ensued.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,
